may_edit: app/src/lib/backup/relayBackup.ts (BackupScheduler retry branch, getBackupRelays, publishBackup relay lookup call)
must_not_edit: BackupScheduler.markDirty / markBackupDirty / activateBackupScheduler (dirty-mark semantics; separate item backup-dirty-mark-lost-on-early-reload)

behaviour: C1: the first failed publish before the scheduler's first success is retried after 5 s; the retry is granted once per scheduler and does not consume the 5-retry budget.
C2: after the early retry (or after any success), failures follow the unchanged 30 s / 2 min / 10 min x3 schedule.
C3: a successful first attempt schedules nothing extra (success path unchanged).

C4: on the publish path, within 60 s of a timed-out relay-list fetch for the same pubkey, it skips the fetch and uses the currently configured relays (getEffectiveRelays() read at call time). No remembered relay list. The lookup path always fetches.
C5: a complete fetch clears the timeout mark; a timed-out fetch's partial list is used for that call only.
C6: privacy: the event (kind 30078, NIP-44 to self, d=few) and the set of reachable relays are unchanged; memo is in-memory and per pubkey.
C7: a publish timeout (indeterminate) is retried exactly like a refusal (current semantics).
non_goals: No change to NDK connect / fetch / publish timeouts.
No change to dirty-mark or debounce semantics.
deviations_from_finding: Success signal 'first backup within 15 s' is met except when the relays stay unresponsive for the whole first attempt (~13 s): then the backup lands at ~18 s (was ~43 s+). Meeting 15 s there would need shorter NDK/fetch timeouts on the backup path (open question).
